content.title: About
content.content: Beef, sandwich steak (651) is a thin cut of meat taken from the tenderloin or chuck of a cow. It has a mild flavor, moderate fat content, and cooks quickly, making it ideal for hot sandwiches, burgers, and fast‑cook dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sandwich steaks are usually sliced 1–1.5 cm thick to ensure rapid cooking.
They are a staple in fast‑food outlets because they stay juicy when cooked fast.
Beef provides all essential amino acids, making it a complete protein source.
Traditionally these steaks are grilled or pan‑seared with a little oil.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The steak supplies high‑quality protein needed for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It provides vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals aid immune function and protect against oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets as it contains virtually no sugars.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels; choose lean cuts when possible.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor pathogens; cook to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may have an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Large amounts can exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Quickly sear the sandwich steak on high heat for 1–2 minutes per side, then slice thinly. Use it in hot sandwiches, burger patties, salads, or serve with barbecue sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–4 °C in an airtight container for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in a bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 6 months. Thaw in the fridge before cooking.
